Re: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Member: Quinn Grant
Member ID: W914144325
Reference Number: POC-A7C9BA9551-23896
Requested Service: Total ankle replacement, CPT 27702
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-22

To the Cigna Appeals Review Team:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as described in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22. The stated reason for denial was that "the requested procedure does not meet the plan's criteria for medical necessity." I am submitting this appeal within the 180-day deadline stated in the notice, which is 2027-02-18.

I have identified that Cigna's applicable coverage document for this procedure is Medical Coverage Policy 0285, "Total Ankle Arthroplasty/Replacement" (Coverage Policy Number 0285), which lists CPT 27702 as a covered code when its medical-necessity criteria are met. That policy states:

"Total ankle arthroplasty/replacement with a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)-approved/cleared device is considered medically necessary as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis when ALL of the following criteria have been met: individual is skeletally mature; presence of ONE of the following in the affected ankle: severe inflammatory arthritis (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis), severe osteoarthritis, post-traumatic arthritis; individual has moderate to severe ankle pain that: is function-limiting at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration, interferes with the ability to carry out age appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment; failure of at least six months of conservative therapy (i.e., anti-inflammatory medications, orthotic devices, activity modification, physical therapy); individual has NONE of the following contraindications to total ankle arthroplasty: active infection, insufficient bone/osteonecrosis, loss of musculature in the affected limb/insufficient ligament support, vascular insufficiency in the affected limb, Charcot's or other peripheral neuropathy, neurological impairment, severe ankle deformity precluding proper alignment, malalignment or severe deformity of involved or adjacent anatomic structures (e.g. hindfoot, forefoot, knee), absence of medial or lateral malleolus, or both, poor skin conditions secondary to surgical scars or trauma."

The policy further states: "Total ankle arthroplasty/replacement for any other indication is considered not medically necessary."

I respectfully submit that my clinical record satisfies each of the affirmative criteria in this policy, as follows:

1. Skeletally mature individual: [Records provided to me do not state my date of birth or an explicit statement of skeletal maturity — please confirm this element from the chart maintained by Dr. Reyes, or I will supplement this appeal with that confirmation.]

2. Qualifying diagnosis in the affected ankle: Weight-bearing ankle radiographs obtained 2026-07-07 show tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. These findings are consistent with severe osteoarthritis of the tibiotalar joint. [The specific diagnostic label/ICD-10 code used by Dr. Reyes is not included in the clinical summary provided to me; I ask that the plan review the imaging report and surgeon's diagnosis directly, and I will supplement this appeal with the exact diagnosis code if needed.]

3. Moderate to severe, function-limiting ankle pain of at least three months' duration: I have experienced 14 months of progressive ankle pain, unrelieved by rest. On examination I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to two blocks of walking distance — squarely within the policy's example of function-limiting pain "at short distances (e.g., ... limiting activity to two city blocks ...)." This pain and functional limitation have persisted well beyond the three-month threshold in the policy and interfere with my ability to carry out ordinary daily activities.

4. Failure of at least six months of conservative therapy: I completed 12 weeks (18 visits) of supervised physical therapy focused on ankle strengthening and balance, from 2026-04-09 to 2026-07-02, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. In addition, I was treated with NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-18 that provided only 4 weeks of partial relief. Taken together, this course of anti-inflammatory medication, activity modification, and formal physical therapy meets and exceeds the six-month conservative-therapy requirement in the policy, and it has failed to resolve my symptoms.

5. Absence of listed contraindications: The clinical summary confirms no active infection. My exam did not identify vascular insufficiency, neuropathy, neurological impairment, severe deformity precluding alignment, malalignment of adjacent structures, absence of the malleolus, or poor skin condition; positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion were the reported exam findings, with no mention of any of the disqualifying conditions listed in the policy. [If Dr. Reyes's chart contains additional specific statements addressing insufficient bone/osteonecrosis, ligament/muscle insufficiency, or skin condition, I ask that those be treated as part of the record; I will supplement this appeal with any additional documentation the plan requires on these specific points.]

Based on the above, my clinical presentation meets the medical-necessity criteria set out in Cigna Coverage Policy 0285 for total ankle arthroplasty (CPT 27702) as an alternative to ankle arthrodesis. I ask that the denial be reversed and that prior authorization be granted.

I am enclosing (or asking my surgeon's office to submit directly) the following supporting records:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-04-09 to 2026-07-02, 18 visits)
- Medication history documenting 6 months of NSAID use and the 2026-05-18 corticosteroid injection
- Weight-bearing ankle radiograph report dated 2026-07-07
- Office examination notes documenting antalgic gait, two-block walking limitation, positive provocative testing, and pain-limited range of motion
- Operative plan/letter of medical necessity from Reyes, MD

If Cigna's determination relied on any specific unmet criterion from Coverage Policy 0285 that was not identified in the original denial notice, I request written clarification of exactly which criterion was found unmet, along with a copy of the specific policy version and clinical rationale applied to my case, so that I may address it directly.

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and provide the expected timeframe for a decision. I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions.

Sincerely,

Quinn Grant
Member ID: W914144325
